items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: And I had a chance to play with the greatest of the greats: Gene Krupa, Buddy Rich, Cozy Cole, George Wettling, everyone was there, Lionel Hampton was there with his band, it was unbelievable.

ctx.x: Yeah. Tell me about working in this weird Metropole stage. That must have been kind of different to be all standing in a row.

Right. Wall to wall jazz they called it. All in single file. We had one drummer at this end of the stage, Monk, we had another drummer at that end of the stage, we had two little upright pianos, they were like spinets, that’s what they call them. And we had two sets of drums. It was a very strange thing but we all became acclimated to it. I know I did after being there for ten years. And I had a chance to play with the greatest of the greats: Gene Krupa, Buddy Rich, Cozy Cole, George Wettling, everyone was there,…

Tell me about working with your own group. How did the musical scene change for you over the years? I mean you’ve always managed to find work. But has there been a number of years, or a decade, where things have been tougher?
